user_questions.question: 1) Where should catering orders live? (A) new Catering_Order__c object related to Storefront__c and Account (recommended; nothing in the org represents catering, Marketing_Event__c.Type__c has no Catering value, Order has 0 records); (B) Marketing_Event__c with a new Catering Type__c value using Expected_Attendance__c; (C) standard Order. 2) What does 'need a deposit' mean? (A) a deposit amount > 0 must be entered on save, with a separate Deposit Paid flag tracked (recommended); (B) the deposit must be marked paid before save; (C) both.
user_questions.simulated_answer: 1) A new Catering Order object with headcount, event date, deposit amount and deposit paid; headcount must be at least 20; related to Storefront and the customer Account. 2) Track a deposit amount and whether it is paid; enforcement not specified (no preference; use your recommended default).

skill_friction: Two wrong AskCoworker claims (new object 'inherits' parent OWD; no non-admin profile has View All Data) triggered the verify-everything rule late in the run; SKILL.md does not say whether AskCoworker proposals that are really platform-behavior statements (e.g. OWD inheritance) count as 'wrong claims' toward the threshold.
The T template for a 12-row inventory timed out at 300 words; the '>8 changes -> API names only, split R' guidance covers R but not T, so T needed a narrowed retry.

Step 2 allows skipping D2 only if D1 answered it; for a brand-new object the D2 template's focus (behavior on existing objects) is only loosely relevant, and it is unclear whether D2 should target the parent objects.

The user answer covered which fields exist (deposit amount/paid) but not which is enforced; SKILL.md's rule for partially answered questions (map to matching option, tagged assumption) was applicable but it is ambiguous whether the chosen enforcement is a user decision or an assumption.

Validation-rule blank handling for number comparisons is not documented in the reference files; spec-format requires stating blank results for formulas, but validation rules have no BlankAsZero setting, forcing a hedge.
